issues.title: [Usage]: Inconsistent Embedding Outputs for Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B Across vLLM Versions – How to Fix/Pin Unique Vector Values
issues.body:
### Your current environment

The output of `python collect_env.py`

### How would you like to use vllm on ascend

I am deploying the Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B model using vllm serve. I noticed that when using different versions of vLLM to serve the exact same model with identical inputs, the output embedding vectors are slightly different, resulting in a cosine similarity of less than 1.0.
Since embedding models should be deterministic, I would like to understand the root cause of this discrepancy and find a reliable way to fix/pin the unique vector values

issues.title: [Bug]: VL models in text-only mode incorrectly skip first-layer SP AllGather with FlashComm1
issues.body:
### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>The output of `python collect_env.py`</summary>

```text
Your output of above commands here
```

</details>


### 🐛 Describe the bug

When FlashComm1 / sequence parallelism (SP) is enabled for a vision-language model, the first language-model attention layer always skips the SP AllGather based on the static model architecture (`is_vl_model()`).

This is incorrect when the VL model is running in a text-only configuration, such as `--language-model-only`, where the first-layer input may come from the model's own embedding layer.

In this case, the embedding output is ReduceScatter-ed by the SP path before entering the first transformer layer, so the first-layer input is already TP-sharded and must be AllGather-ed before the column-parallel attention projection.

The issue is not model-specific. We reproduced the same behavior with both Qwen3.5 and MiniMax-M3.

## Current behavior

The current implementation in `SequenceColumnParallelOp.apply_impl()` is:

```python
need_all_gather = not (
    extract_layer_index(self.layer.prefix) == 0
    and is_vl_model()
    and "attn" in self.prefix
)
```

Therefore, for any VL architecture, the first attention layer skips AllGather regardless of the actual runtime layout of `input_`.

However, `is_vl_model()` only describes the model architecture. It does not indicate whether the current first-layer input is:

1. an SP-sharded tensor produced by the model embedding layer, or
2. a full-sequence precomputed embedding produced by the multimodal input path.

These two cases require different collective behavior.

---

## Reproduction with Qwen3.5

The issue can be reproduced with Qwen3.5 in language-model-only mode with FlashComm1 enabled.

Example configuration:

```bash
export ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1
export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE="AIV"
export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=1024
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1
export TASK_QUEUE_ENABLE=1

vllm serve /path/to/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-w8a8-mtp \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8000 \
  --data-parallel-size 1 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --seed 1024 \
  --quantization ascend \
  --served-model-name qwen3.5 \
  --max-num-seqs 128 \
  --max-model-len 262144 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --enforce-eager \
  --additional-config '{
      "enable_cpu_binding": true,
      "enable_flashcomm1": true,
      "multistream_overlap_shared_expert": false
  }' \
  --language-model-only
```

With `--language-model-only`, multimodal inputs are disabled, but the resolved architecture is still a VL architecture, so `is_vl_model()` remains true.

With TP=2 and FlashComm1 enabled, the model embedding output goes through SP ReduceScatter.

Observed tensor flow:

```text
Embedding output:
(128, 2048)

After SP ReduceScatter:
(64, 2048)

First-layer SequenceColumnParallelOp input:
(64, 2048)

is_vl_model():
True

Current need_all_gather:
False
```

The first layer therefore keeps the sharded tensor instead of restoring the full token dimension.

The execution later fails because different parts of the model operate on inconsistent token dimensions.

For example, in our reproduction:

```text
[SP_DEBUG_RS]
input.shape=(128, 2048)
output.shape=(64, 2048)
effective_sp=True

[SP_DEBUG_COL_BEFORE]
prefix=language_model.model.layers.0.linear_attn.in_proj_qkvz
input.shape=(64, 2048)
is_vl=True
need_all_gather=False
```

A later MoE operation then encounters inconsistent token dimensions.

If the first-layer AllGather is temporarily forced on for diagnosis, the expected shape is restored:

```text
(64, 2048)
    |
    | TP AllGather
    v
(128, 2048)
```

and the text-only inference path can proceed normally.

---

## Cross-model reproduction with MiniMax-M3

The same issue was also reproduced with MiniMax-M3 under TP=4.

For a text-only configuration, the observed flow was:

```text
Before embedding SP communication:
hidden_states = (1024, 6144)

After embedding ReduceScatter:
hidden_states = (256, 6144)

positions = (1024,)
```

At the first attention layer:

```text
input.shape=(256, 6144)
is_vl=True
need_all_gather=False
```

The missing AllGather causes the attention tensors to remain on the local SP shard while `positions` still describes the full token sequence:

```text
positions.shape      = (1024,)
hidden_states.shape  = (256, 6144)
qkv.shape            = (256, 2304)
```

This eventually results in a RoPE/token-dimension mismatch.

The RoPE failure is only a downstream symptom. The actual problem occurs earlier when the first-layer SP AllGather is incorrectly skipped.

---

## Why AllGather cannot simply be enabled unconditionally

The opposite case also exists.

When the multimodal path is enabled, the model runner can provide precomputed `inputs_embeds`. In this case, the first language-model layer already receives the full token sequence.

For example, with MiniMax-M3 TP=4:

```text
First-layer input:
(64, 6144)
```

If AllGather is forced unconditionally:

```text
(64, 6144)
    |
    | TP AllGather
    v
(256, 6144)
```

while:

```text
positions.shape = (64,)
```

This again produces an invalid token layout.

Similarly, with Qwen3.5 TP=2, forcing AllGather for a normal multimodal input changes:

```text
(128, 2048)
    |
    | TP AllGather
    v
(256, 2048)
```

even though the input was already full-sequence.

Therefore neither of the following is correct:

```text
Always skip first-layer AllGather for VL models
```

or:

```text
Always perform first-layer AllGather for VL models
```

---

## Expected behavior

The first-layer collective should depend on the runtime layout/source of the first-layer input rather than only on whether the architecture is a VL model.

The expected behavior is:

| First-layer input path | Runtime layout | FlashComm1/SP | First-layer AllGather |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Model embedding | SP-sharded | Enabled | Required |
| Precomputed `inputs_embeds` | Full sequence | Enabled | Must be skipped |

Conceptually:

```text
Text-only / model-embedding path:

input_ids
   |
   v
model embedding
   |
   v
SP ReduceScatter
   |
   v
[N / TP, hidden]
   |
   | first-layer AllGather
   v
[N, hidden]
```

while the precomputed embedding path is:

```text
precomputed inputs_embeds
   |
   v
[N, hidden]
   |
   | no first-layer AllGather
   v
[N, hidden]
```

The decision therefore needs a runtime signal describing whether the first-layer input is actually SP-sharded.

---

## Summary

The current first-layer optimization uses:

```text
is_vl_model()
```

as a proxy for the runtime layout of the first-layer input.

This assumption does not hold when the same VL architecture can run through both:

- a model-embedding/text-only path, and
- a precomputed-embedding/multimodal path.

As a result:

```text
VL architecture + model embedding + FlashComm1/SP
```

can incorrectly skip the required first-layer AllGather and fail because of downstream token-dimension mismatches.

This appears to be a framework-level issue rather than a MiniMax-M3- or Qwen3.5-specific issue.

issues.title: [Performance]: The qwen3-vl model does not enable the mrope fusion operator.
issues.body:
### Proposal to improve performance

#### Mrope Section Info
| model | mrope section | reference link |
| - | - | - |
| Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct | [16, 24, 24] | https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct/blob/main/config.json#L54-L58 |
| Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct | [24, 20, 20] | https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct/blob/main/config.json#L26-L30 |

#### Codes
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/blob/1b5d5abf865f57742aab2d22dd6737af719c124a/vllm_ascend/ops/rotary_embedding.py#L504-L506

#### Problem
At present, the mrope operator only supports the mrope section of qwen2.5-vl, but the mrope section of qwen3-vl is different, and the inability to use the mrope operator will result in rollback. We hope to increase the shape of qwen3-vl so that the qwen3-vl model can also use the mrope operator

### Report of performance regression
Compare the performance of qwen3-vl-8b model before and after using mrope operator
### before
| images num | QPS |
| - | - | 
|1 | 0.90|
|5 |0.52|
|10| 0.45|

Performance after PR modification #5673 
#### after
| images num | QPS |
| - | - | 
|1 | 1.46|
|5 |1.1|
|10| 0.84|


### Misc discussion on performance

_No response_
